findings.title: Attacker-controlled dictionary keys can pollute Object.prototype
findings.summary: Dictionaries built from untrusted plist/config keys assigned values with plain-object semantics, so a key such as __proto__ could mutate Object.prototype and inject values the analyzer would read as configuration.

severity.rationale: A malicious PR author controls plist and app.config keys; successful pollution alters analyzer-visible configuration and can corrupt downstream object behavior, but does not achieve code execution on the runner.

confidence.rationale: Reproduced with a minimal fixture: out['__proto__'] = {NSPrivacyTracking: 'INJECTED'} made out['NSPrivacyTracking'] resolve to the injected value.

findings.remediation: Build all attacker-keyed dictionaries with Object.create(null) (applied in src/parsers/plist.ts, src/parsers/expoConfig.ts walkPartial/evaluateNode/deepMerge, src/config/schema.ts parseRuleOverrides/parseSdkCategories, src/rules/sdkCategories.ts).

validation.summary: Confirmed vulnerable before fix with a standalone Node reproduction; confirmed fixed after change with a dedicated security test (test/security/malicious.test.ts '__proto__ keys do not pollute objects or inject values').

attackPath.summary: PR author commits PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy (or app.config.js) containing a __proto__ dictionary key; the plist/app-config parser assigns it to a plain object, mutating its prototype; subsequent field lookups (e.g., root['NSPrivacyTracking']) return attacker-supplied values, injecting analyzer conclusions.
attackPath.reachability: Reachable from the Action and CLI on any PR that includes such a file, because the file is inside the relevant-path set.

rootCause.summary: Plain-object assignment of attacker-controlled keys without null prototypes.

preventiveControls: Null-prototype objects for all attacker-keyed dictionaries

findings.title: Oversized file content can be read into memory before the size limit is enforced
findings.summary: The local git provider and the GitHub blob fallback fetched full blob content before buildSnapshot applied max-file-size-bytes, so a multi-gigabyte file in a PR could transiently exhaust runner/CLI memory.

severity.rationale: Local-CLI DoS potential only; the GitHub contents API inlines only small files, and the fallback path is bounded after the fix. Requires a large file in the relevant-path set.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace: fetchBlob/getFile read content before any maxFileSize comparison.

findings.remediation: Check declared size (git cat-file -s / contents API size / stat) against max-file-size-bytes before reading content, and mark oversized files as truncated coverage gaps (applied).

validation.summary: Verified the size guard now short-circuits before the read in fetchBlob, fetchWorkingFile, and GitHub getFile; oversized-file coverage-gap behavior is covered by test/unit/buildSnapshot.test.ts.

attackPath.summary: PR author adds a very large relevant file; the CLI or Action reads it fully into a Buffer before discarding it, transiently using size-bounded memory far above the configured limit.
attackPath.reachability: Reachable from the CLI and Action whenever the changed-file set includes a large relevant path.

rootCause.summary: Content read preceded the size check in the provider layer.

preventiveControls: Size check before read in all three providers (git blob, working tree, GitHub contents/blob fallback)

findings.title: Finding base/head state values were not passed through the redactor
findings.summary: candidateToFinding redacted evidence but copied baseState/headState verbatim, so a credential that appeared inside a compared configuration value (e.g., an exotic purpose string) could be echoed in JSON/markdown output.

severity.rationale: ARD006 never populates state fields, and other rules' state values are configuration strings; the exposure requires a secret placed inside a compared config field, but defense-in-depth redaction is cheap.

confidence.rationale: Code path confirmed; exploitability depends on rules populating state with secret-bearing content.

findings.remediation: Route baseState/headState through redacted() before building Finding (applied).

validation.summary: Confirmed engine.ts now redacts both state fields; redaction unit tests still pass.

attackPath.summary: A compared configuration value contains a private-credential-shaped string; the finding's state fields carry it into JSON/summary output unredacted.
attackPath.reachability: Reachable only when a rule populates state with the credential-bearing string.

rootCause.summary: Inconsistent redaction coverage between evidence and state fields.

preventiveControls: Single redaction path for every string field emitted by the engine

findings.title: Non-file contents-API entries were not explicitly skipped
findings.summary: The GitHub contents client only special-cased symlinks; directories and submodules fell through to the blob fallback path, which could raise or fetch unexpected data instead of a clean skip.

severity.rationale: The relevant-path set rarely contains directories/submodules; impact is a noisy error or unnecessary request rather than a security break, and it is now explicitly skipped.

confidence.rationale: Direct source inspection of the contents response handling.

findings.remediation: Skip any contents-API entry whose type is not 'file' and record it as a coverage gap (applied).

validation.summary: Code now returns a symlink-style skip for dir/submodule entries before the blob fallback.

attackPath.summary: A PR path matching the relevant set resolves to a submodule/directory; the client would otherwise attempt a blob fetch of a non-blob object.
attackPath.reachability: Low; relevant-path patterns rarely match directories.

rootCause.summary: Incomplete type handling for contents-API responses.

preventiveControls: Explicit skip for all non-file contents entries
